newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexican ports reopened in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexican ports reopened in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: Two Mexican ports on the Gulf of Mexico reopened on Sunday after being closed Saturday because of strong winds and choppy seas, the Communications and Transport Ministry said.
The ports of Tampico and Altamira in southern Tamaulipas state had been closed on Saturday.
But the ministry, in its regular ports bulletin issued on Sunday, still issued a 24-hour warning of caution for ships off Tamaulipas state.
The gulf coast of Tamaulipas state runs from the the U.S.-Mexican border at Brownsville-Matamoros down to Tampico.
The Tampico port is important for the export of petroleum, grains and other products destined for the southern United States.
